scope: Theorem 4.1 (Fixed caps with a nonzero pairing) of the manuscript “Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere” (preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 306 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ee916c92b825a868), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 39. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are two fixed compact caps C− and C+ with common rational boundary Y2, fixed determinant data trivialized at that boundary, and finite collections of integral point and surface probes in their interiors with the following properties. (i) Each cap has H1(C±; Z) = 0 and b+(C±) > 0. Each contains a square-zero copy of A on which the determinant class evaluates as 1, and a tight genus-two surface of square two. (ii) Each cap has one additional, separate exceptional summand. The determinant evaluates as zero on its exceptional sphere, and every probe is supported in the old part of the cap. (iii) For suitable generic cap data and small ordinary Floer data at the rational boundary, the cut counts give a rational cycle x and a rational cocycle y on the irreducible determinant-one Floer complex, with yx ̸= 0. (4.2) Fixed integral multiples of these are an integral cycle and cocycle. (iv) The total real degree z of all cap probes is fixed. Reducible cap limits in any of the bounded charge ranges used below are excluded by the cap period choices. The period choices admit the finite isolation extensions of Proposition 7.9. The cycle and cocycle can be recomputed with the final cap data used in Section 5; their pairing is the same nonzero closed Donaldson count, up to the fixed normalization and orientation sign.
